title: BIGX - GPU-accelerated dynamic programming for buffer insertion (timing violations)
problem: Buffer insertion for timing violation recovery involves solving a large dynamic programming problem to determine optimal buffer placement on signal nets. Traditional CPU-based approaches are computationally expensive and slow.
motivation: GPU acceleration can parallelize the dynamic programming computation across many nets simultaneously, dramatically reducing runtime for timing closure optimization.
method: BIGX takes Van Ginneken's buffer insertion algorithm—which determines where to place buffers (signal-boosting circuit elements) to fix timing violations—and runs it on GPU instead of CPU. Instead of computing sequentially, it breaks the problem into independent subproblems that GPU threads can solve in parallel, while optimizing how data flows through GPU memory to avoid the bottlenecks that slow down CPU versions.
key_novelty: Parallel GPU implementation of Van Ginneken's buffer insertion algorithm for timing-violation recovery.
contributions: GPU parallelization of Van Ginneken's buffer insertion algorithm
Scalable timing violation recovery for large designs
limitations: GPU acceleration benefits may plateau for designs with fewer nets or timing paths, and GPU memory constraints could limit applicability to very large designs.
